questions: Does max_error fall below 0.06 m on the oval and s-bend, and which track still ends first?
Does steering_oscillation rise above the 0.07 baseline with the narrower track and lighter body? If so, is it because of the wheel track or the mass?
Is line_loss_events still 0? If not, which track and at what max_error?
What is progress on each track now, and does any run reach progress above 0.5?
Does the robot get close to the 1.5 m/s speed needed for completion, or is it limited by the lighter body or narrower track?
feedback_request.requested_changes_if_any: If steering_oscillation exceeds about 0.1 with max_error still near 0.06 m, revert wheel_track to 0.12 m and keep the lighter body to isolate the inertia effect. If max_error improves but the robot still goes off track, try wheel_track 0.09 m.

intent: Keep the sensing layout that removed line loss (±0.05 m spread, 16 mm footprint, y = 0.04 m). Make the body more responsive by reducing yaw inertia (mass 0.7 to 0.5 kg, body length 0.16 to 0.12 m) and raising turn rate per wheel difference (wheel track 0.12 to 0.10 m). The aim is to cut max_error below the 0.06 m off-track limit and let the robot cover more of the track.
learning: Iteration 1 showed that widening the sensor spread and footprint removed line loss but not the off-track failure. So the failure is in how the body responds, not in what the sensors see. Next I test whether reducing yaw inertia and turn-track width reduces max_error. Key measurements: max_error per track, steering_oscillation against the 0.07 baseline, and progress per track.
rationale: The iteration 1 race (entityR2A, 26.64) removed line loss: line_loss_events is now 0 on all three tracks, down from 1 per run. Every run still ends off_track, with max_error about 0.06 m (the off-track limit) and progress of only 0.035 to 0.11. So the line is no longer lost. The robot drifts off while the tape is still under the sensors, which points to a tracking response problem, not a sensing-coverage problem. Steering oscillation is unchanged at about 0.07, so the 16 mm footprint is not causing jitter and the ±0.05 m spread is not the limiting factor. The off-track limit is max(0.06, 0.0125 + body_width/4). Body width 0.18 would only give 0.0575, below the 0.06 floor, so body width cannot buy margin and I keep 0.12. What remains is how quickly the body turns and how much inertia it has. Yaw inertia is mass*(L²+W²)/12. I lower it by reducing mass from 0.7 to 0.5 kg and body length from 0.16 to 0.12 m, so the same wheel difference turns the robot faster and it can correct drift before reaching 0.06 m. I narrow wheel_track from 0.12 to 0.10 m, which raises turn rate per unit of wheel difference by about 20%, so the controller's fixed 350 PWM per turn unit has more effect. Sensors stay at ±0.05 m, y = 0.04, 16 mm, which the feedback shows is giving zero line loss. Wheel radius stays 0.03 m to keep the speed needed for a 3 s finish. Expected result: max_error falls below 0.06 m, progress rises above 0.11, and some runs reach progress above 0.5. Risk: a narrower track and lighter body may increase oscillation, which I will check against the 0.07 baseline.
